sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

sparse x INT8 factorial. Fresh session. Read predictions.md Part C (C.1, C.2, C.3) — FROZEN: formats,
calibration rule, INT8 selection rule, sparse operating points, accounting fields. Also read
results/SCHEMA.md, results/partc_selection.json, code/lab3/{bench,models,evaln,compact,prune}.py.
uv only; CPU; frozen threads and latency protocol (20 warm-up, 200 timed, median+IQR, bs1+bs256 for
fmnist, full graph for Cora, RSS in fresh subprocess). Never weaken tests. Never select using test.

1. Backend support report -> results/precision_support.md. Probe on THIS machine and torch 2.15:
   torch.backends.quantized.supported_engines; which quantization APIs exist and work
   (torch.ao.quantization eager quantize_dynamic / prepare+convert, FX prepare_fx/convert_fx, PT2E with
   an available quantizer, torchao if installed — do NOT add torchao unless needed; if you add any
   dependency use `uv add` and record why); whether nn.Linear / Conv2d / GCNConv(.lin) run in fp16 and
   bf16 on CPU (check output dtypes and whether kernels exist or upcast); whether quantized
   linear/conv kernels exist for qnnpack. Every probe result is a row in the report with the evidence
   (command + output). Classify unsupported cases (e.g. unsupported_backend, unsupported_op,
   deprecated_api).
2. Conversions (code/lab3/precision.py), each from the seed-0 dense parent, for all 3 archs:
   fp16, bf16, dynamic INT8, static INT8 (calibrated with splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy inputs only /
   Cora full-graph features only — record calib size and rule in each row), simulated weight-only INT4
   (per-output-channel symmetric [-8,7], fp32 scales, 2 values packed per uint8 on disk, dequantize to
   fp32 for compute; decide once whether dequantization is inside the timed region, document, apply
   identically; label runtime_status "simulated_non_native").
   For the GCN: if a format cannot be applied to GCNConv, try applying it to the projection (.lin) only
   and record exactly which ops ran in reduced precision; if impossible, write a classified
   unsupported row.
3. Every Part C row (part="C", phase="precision" or "factorial") must contain: stored_precision,
   compute_precision, accumulator_precision (per layer table + summary), val/test acc, actual
   serialized bytes on disk (state of the converted model / packed file), latency, rss,
   frac_macs_reduced_precision (from the per-layer MAC table: MACs of layers that actually executed a
   reduced-precision kernel / total MACs), reload_equivalence {tolerance, max_abs_diff, passed}, and
   parent_run_id. Unsupported conversions still get a row (status "unsupported", classified reason).
4. Tests: reload of each saved converted artifact reproduces logits within the explicit tolerance
   (0 for exact formats; documented tolerance otherwise); INT4 pack/unpack is bit-exact; INT4 values in
   [-8,7]; calibration uses only fmnist_calib_idx inputs (assert ⊂ train split); a test that
   frac_macs_reduced_precision is 0 for fp32 and 1.0 for a model whose every layer ran quantized.
5. Select the best supported INT8 method per architecture by the frozen C.1 rule (validation only; ties
   within one val example -> lower latency); write results/int8_selection.json with the evidence.
6. Factorial (12 conditions): for each arch, dense FP32 (parent), sparse FP32 (the C.3 pilot checkpoint
   from partc_selection.json), dense INT8 (selected method), sparse+INT8 (same method applied to the
   sparse model). For sparse rows report nonzero count before/after INT8 (do zeros survive?), the INT8
   file size, and a sparse-INT8 storage size (int8 values + int32 CSR indices + scales) labelled
   runtime-unsupported unless a real kernel exists. Write results/factorial.csv.
7. Figures: figures/precision_size_latency.png (per arch: bytes on disk vs latency, one point per
   format, unsupported formats listed in the caption) and figures/factorial.png (2x2 per arch:
   accuracy, bytes, latency). One legend each, font >= 8, assert non-empty panels. Captions in
   figures/CAPTIONS.md.
8. results/partc_summary.md: tables of all standalone results and the factorial, raw run_ids included.
9. `uv run pytest -q`.
Report: support matrix, standalone table, the INT8 selection, factorial table, test output, and
anomalies (e.g. reduced-precision slower than fp32, frac_macs < 1 for a "quantized" model). Don't interpret.

# Lab 3 — Predictions and Frozen Design Decisions

Each section is dated and was written **before** the runs it governs. Sections are
append-only: later corrections are added as dated amendments, never by editing a frozen
section.

---

## Part A — Dense reference models (frozen 2026-11-09, before any training)

### A.1 Frozen design

**Hardware / software.** Apple M4 Pro (12 CPU cores), 24 GB RAM, macOS. Python 3.12,
PyTorch 2.15.0, torchvision 0.29.2, torch_geometric 2.8.1, NumPy 2.5.4. Package
management with `uv` (`pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`). **CPU only for every arm**; no MPS.

**Threads.** `torch.set_num_threads(4)` and `torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)` for all
training, evaluation, and benchmarking.

**Data splits (created once, saved to `splits/`, reused by every arm).**
- Fashion-MNIST: official 60k train / 10k test. From the 60k train set, a stratified
  5,000-image validation set (500 per class) is drawn once with split seed 12345; the
  remaining 55,000 images are the training set. The 10k official test set is the test set.
  Saved as index files plus a SHA-256 of the index arrays.
- Cora: the standard Planetoid public split (140 train / 500 val / 1000 test nodes), saved
  as node-index files with a SHA-256. The graph (2,708 nodes, 10,556 directed edges) is
  never modified by any compression arm.
- Inputs: Fashion-MNIST normalized with mean/std computed on the 55k training split only.
  Cora features row-normalized (standard GCN preprocessing).

**Architectures.**
| Model | Definition | Params (computed) |
|---|---|---|
| MLP | 784→256→128→10, ReLU, no dropout | 235,146 |
| CNN | Conv(1→16, 5×5, pad 2)→ReLU→MaxPool2 → Conv(16→32, 5×5)→ReLU→MaxPool2 → FC(800→128)→ReLU → FC(128→10) | 117,066 |
| GCN | GCNConv(1433→16)→ReLU→Dropout(0.5) → GCNConv(16→7) | 23,063 |

No BatchNorm anywhere (keeps INT8 conversion and structured surgery unambiguous).

**Training.**
- MLP and CNN: Adam, lr 1e-3, weight decay 0, batch size 128, cross-entropy, max **30
  epochs**.
- GCN: Adam, lr 0.01, weight decay 5e-4, full-batch, cross-entropy on the 140 train nodes,
  max **300 epochs**.

**Early stopping / checkpoint selection (validation only).** After each epoch, evaluate
validation accuracy. Keep the checkpoint with the highest validation accuracy; ties go to
the lower validation loss, then to the earlier epoch. Stop when validation accuracy has not
improved for **5 epochs** (MLP, CNN) or **50 epochs** (GCN), or at the max epoch count. The
test set is evaluated only on the selected checkpoint and never feeds back into any choice.

**Seeds.** Each run sets Python `random`, NumPy, and PyTorch seeds to the run seed and logs
it.
- Pilot seed: **0**. Produces the canonical dense checkpoint per architecture. Every
  compression arm starts from it, and the full Part B pilot matrix uses it.
- Confirmatory seeds: **1, 2, 3**. Used (a) to train three replica dense baselines per
  architecture, which report seed variance only and are never used as compression parents,
  and (b) in Part B to repeat the selected operating points. There the seed controls
  fine-tuning shuffle order and dropout, and the parent is always the canonical seed-0
  checkpoint.
- The split seed 12345 is separate from these and is never changed.

**Sanity targets (test accuracy).** MLP ≥ 82%, CNN ≥ 87%, GCN ≥ 65%. A miss is diagnosed,
and the cause is recorded. The target is not lowered.

**Latency protocol.** `torch.inference_mode()`, model in `eval()`. 20 warm-up and 200
timed iterations, timed with `time.perf_counter_ns`. Report the median and IQR. Batch sizes
are **1** and **256** for Fashion-MNIST, and one full-graph forward pass for Cora. Peak RSS
is measured in a fresh subprocess per benchmark.

**Stopping rule for agent work.** If a baseline misses its target after one diagnosed fix,
or any required test fails twice after a fix, work stops and the issue is reviewed before
continuing. Tests are never weakened to pass.

### A.2 Predictions

**Parameter count: MLP (235k) > CNN (117k) > GCN (23k).**
*Mechanism:* the MLP's first layer alone (784×256 ≈ 201k) dominates its count. The CNN
shares 5×5 kernels across positions, so its convolutions are tiny (≈13k), and most of its
parameters sit in FC(800→128) (≈103k). The GCN has a 16-wide hidden layer, so nearly all
of its parameters are the 1433×16 input projection.

**Dense checkpoint size: MLP (~0.94 MB) > CNN (~0.47 MB) > GCN (~0.09 MB).**
*Mechanism:* FP32 state dicts are about 4 bytes × params, plus a few KB of pickle/zip
overhead. The overhead is proportionally largest for the GCN, so its ratio to the others
will be slightly above the raw parameter ratio. The Cora graph is data, not checkpoint.

**Training time to the selected checkpoint: CNN > MLP > GCN.**
*Mechanism:* per image, the CNN does about 1.7M MACs (conv2 alone is about 1.28M), against
0.235M for the MLP. That is about 7× more compute over the same 55k images per epoch,
partly offset by better-optimized conv kernels. The GCN trains full-batch on 2,708 nodes.
Each epoch is one sparse aggregation plus a 2708×1433×16 projection, so 300 epochs should
take seconds, against minutes for the image models.

**Sensitivity to compression (most to least): GCN > CNN > MLP.**
*Mechanism:*
- *GCN:* it has a 16-dimensional bottleneck and only 140 labelled nodes for fine-tuning.
  Every remaining weight carries a large share of the representation, and recovery data is
  scarce. Most of its input-projection weights belong to rare bag-of-words features, so
  moderate unstructured sparsity should be tolerated. At high sparsity, and for structured
  removal of hidden features, I expect the sharpest collapse.
- *CNN:* convolution weights are reused at every spatial position, so pruning one conv
  weight perturbs many activations. Global magnitude pruning should mostly remove FC
  weights, which buffers it, but structured channel pruning of a 16/32-channel network
  should hurt.
- *MLP:* it is heavily over-parameterized for Fashion-MNIST. Many first-layer weights
  attach to border pixels with near-constant input, so they carry little signal and should
  prune almost for free up to high sparsity.
- *Precision:* I predict INT8 costs every model < 0.5 pp of accuracy. Simulated INT4 should
  hurt the GCN and CNN more than the MLP, for the same bottleneck and weight-reuse reasons.

**Expected baseline test accuracy:** MLP about 88–89%, CNN about 90–91%, GCN about 80–81%.

---

## Part B — Four forms of sparsity (frozen 2026-11-09, before any pruning run)

### B.1 Common protocol (all four methods)

- **Parent:** every arm starts from the canonical seed-0 dense checkpoint of its
  architecture (`checkpoints/dense/<arch>_seed0.pt`).
- **One-shot pruning,** followed by a fixed fine-tuning budget. There is no iterative
  pruning.
- **Eligible tensors:** the weight matrix/kernel of every Linear, Conv2d, and GCNConv layer,
  including the final classifier. Biases are never pruned, and there are no normalization
  layers.
- **Fine-tuning budget (identical for every method within an architecture):**
  - MLP/CNN: 3 epochs, Adam lr 5e-4, batch 128, frozen 55k training split.
  - GCN: 50 epochs, Adam lr 0.005, weight decay 5e-4, dropout 0.5, 140 training nodes.
  - The fine-tuning checkpoint is the epoch with the best validation accuracy inside that
    budget. Ties go to the later epoch, which is the more-trained model.
- **Masks:** for S1/S3/S4 a binary mask is re-applied after every optimizer step, so pruned
  entries stay exactly zero. Adam state for masked entries is irrelevant because the mask
  is applied to the weights.
- **Measurement stages:** every arm is measured twice: immediately after pruning, before
  any update (`stage=post_prune`), and after fine-tuning (`stage=post_finetune`). Both rows
  carry val/test accuracy, per-layer sparsity, bytes, MACs, latency, and memory.
- **Pilot:** seed 0 for the full 3 × 4 × 4 matrix. In fine-tuning, the seed controls data
  order and dropout.
- **Calibration subset (S3 now, reused in Part C):**
  - Fashion-MNIST: 1,024 images from the **training** split, stratified 102–103 per class,
    drawn once with seed 12345 and saved to `splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy`. The labels are
    training labels.
  - Cora: the 140 training nodes on the full graph.
  - No validation or test labels are ever used for calibration.

### B.2 Method specifications

**S1 Global unstructured magnitude.** Pool all eligible weights across layers, then zero
the fraction *s* with the smallest |w|. Targets: 25/50/75/90%. Achieved sparsity is
reported globally and per tensor.

**S2 Structured group pruning (L1).** Groups and their L1 norms:
- MLP: hidden units of both hidden layers. The norm is the unit's incoming weight row.
- CNN: output channels of conv1 and conv2 (L1 of each filter) and FC1 hidden units.
  Removing conv2 channels also removes the matching FC1 input columns.
- GCN: the 16 hidden features. The norm is the incoming weight column of layer 1.

Ranking is **layer-wise**: each prunable layer removes the same fraction, keeping
k = max(1, round((1 − s)·n)) groups. The classifier output and the input dimension are
never pruned. The model is **physically rebuilt** as a smaller dense model by copying the
surviving rows/columns/bias entries. The target is the fraction of groups removed, and the
achieved value is reported as both group sparsity and parameter sparsity relative to the
dense model. These differ. For example, at s = 90%, GCN keeps round(1.6) = 2 features, so
87.5% of groups are removed.

**S3 First-order saliency (unstructured, global; this choice is fixed).** The score is
|w ⊙ ∂L/∂w|, where L is the mean cross-entropy over the whole calibration subset (one
gradient computed on the dense parent in eval mode, so no dropout). Pool all eligible
weights across layers and zero the lowest-scoring fraction *s*.

**S4 N:M semi-structured.**
- Blocks are M consecutive weights along each row's **reduction (input) dimension**. Conv
  kernels are flattened to [out, in·k·k]. In each block, keep the N largest |w|.
- If the row length is not divisible by M, the final partial block of length r keeps
  ⌈N·r/M⌉ weights.
- **Patterns, chosen before running:** 3:4 (25%), 2:4 (50%), 1:4 (75%), and 1:10 (90%,
  following the instructor's guidance). Every pilot cell is filled by a real run.
- Partial blocks make achieved sparsity slightly below the nominal value for rows with
  remainders: conv1 rows have 25 weights, and GCN layer 1 rows have 1,433. Achieved
  sparsity is reported.
- No cell is filled by copying another run.

### B.3 Confirmatory point selection rule (validation only; fixed before any test result is seen)

For each architecture × method, take the pilot (seed 0) post-fine-tune rows:

1. **Eligible levels:** post-fine-tune validation accuracy ≥ dense seed-0 validation
   accuracy − τ. τ = 1.0 pp for MLP and CNN. τ = 2.0 pp for GCN, whose 500-node validation
   set gives one node = 0.2 pp and a binomial SE of ~1.8 pp.
2. **Choose** the eligible level with the **highest target sparsity**.
3. **Fallback:** if no level is eligible, choose the level with the highest post-fine-tune
   validation accuracy. Ties go to the lower sparsity.
4. **Rerun** the chosen point with seeds 1, 2, 3, using the same parent and budget.

Test accuracy is logged but never read by this rule.

### B.4 Two runtime paths

- **Path 1:** dense PyTorch modules holding zero-valued weights. Run this for every arm.

# Lab 3 `results/runs.jsonl` record schema

Every command (`train`, `eval`, `bench`) appends exactly one JSON object per
attempted run to `results/runs.jsonl` (append-only: lines are never edited or
deleted; a corrected re-bench adds a new line whose `supersedes` lists the
earlier, now-incorrect run_ids). This file documents the fields.

## Identity / linkage

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | str | Unique id for this record: `<arch>-<method>-<UTC timestamp>-<shortuuid>`. |
| `status` | str | `"ok"` or `"failed"`. |
| `reason` | str/null | Failure reason when `status == "failed"`. |
| `part` | str | `"A"` (dense reference). |
| `phase` | str/null | Matrix phase the record belongs to: `"pilot"` for the Part B pilot matrix (seed 0, including the B.6 `dense_ft` control arms) and `"confirm"` for the confirmatory reruns (seeds 1/2/3, B.3). **B2 (2026-11-09, before any pilot-matrix run):** every new Part B record carries `phase`; all earlier records (Part A, and the B1/B1b Part B smoke rows) predate the field and carry `null` in any record written by new code, or no field at all (never edited — the log is append-only). |
| `architecture` | str | `mlp` / `cnn` / `gcn`. |
| `method` | str | `"dense"` for the Part A baseline. |
| `seed` | int | Random seed. |
| `command` | str | `train` / `eval` / `bench`. |
| `parent_run_id` | str/null | For `bench` (and `eval`), the `run_id` of the **training run** that produced the checkpoint being benchmarked. Carried from the checkpoint metadata `run_id`. |
| `supersedes` | list[str] | For a corrected re-bench: the `run_id`s of the earlier bench records for the same (architecture, seed) that are now known to be incorrect (e.g. A1's wrong MAC/byte figures). The old lines remain in the log untouched. |

## Training / selection

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `train_epochs` | int/null | Epochs actually run (may stop early). |
| `finetune_epochs` | int | 0 in Part A. |
| `best_epoch` | int/null | Epoch of the validation-selected checkpoint. |
| `val_acc`, `val_loss` | float/null | Validation accuracy / loss. |
| `test_acc` | float/null | Test accuracy (evaluated only on the selected checkpoint). |

## Size

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `total_params` | int | `sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())`. |
| `nonzero_params` | int | Number of nonzero weight/param elements. For the dense baseline this equals `total_params`; Part B arms report the physically sparse count. |
| `dense_bytes` | int | **Actual on-disk size** (bytes) of a `torch.save(state_dict)` file — the bare state dict (no metadata) written to a temp file, read with `os.path.getsize`. Includes the PyTorch zip/pickle container overhead, so it is slightly larger than `raw_tensor_bytes`. |
| `raw_tensor_bytes` | int | `sum(t.numel() * t.element_size())` over every state_dict tensor — pure payload bytes, no container overhead. |
| `gzip_bytes` | int/null | **P1 (A2 review):** gzip-9 size (bytes) of the `dense_bytes` state_dict file. Reported for **every run, dense included** — it is a property of the dense container, not of a compression method. Null only where a run failed before measuring it. |
| `compressed_bytes` | int/null | **P1 (A2 review):** RESERVED for the **compact-export artifact** (Part B path 2: the genuinely sparse on-disk file — S2 rebuilt dense model, S1/S3 CSR file, S4 packed N:M file). **Null for the dense Part A baseline** (dense has no compact export). Part A `bench` rows record the gzip-9 figure in `gzip_bytes`, not here. |

### Part B (sparsity) additions (Task B1)

Pruning arms (`command == "prune"`, `part == "B"`) append **two rows per arm**,
`stage="post_prune"` and `stage="post_finetune"`, sharing one `arm_id`.
(The pilot driver `uv run python -m lab3 pilot` appends exactly these rows with
`phase="pilot"`, seed 0, one per cell of {mlp,cnn,gcn} x {s1,s2,s3,s4} x
{0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9} plus one `dense_ft` control arm (target 0) per architecture;
failed arms additionally append `stage="failed"` rows. Progress: one line per
arm in `results/pilot_log.txt`; summaries: `results/pilot_summary.csv` (one line
per arm x stage) and `results/pilot_per_layer.csv` (arm, stage, per tensor).)

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `part` | str | `"B"`. |
| `command` | str | `prune`. |
| `stage` | str | `post_prune` / `post_finetune`. |
| `arm_id` | str | Shared by the arm's two rows: `<arch>-<method>-t<target>-seed<seed>-<UTC ts>-<uuid6>`. |
| `method` | str | `s1` / `s2` / `s3` / `s4`. |
| `target_sparsity` | float | Frozen target (0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.9). |
| `achieved_sparsity` | float | Fraction of **eligible weight** elements that are zero (post_prune / post_finetune each). |
| `achieved_param_sparsity` | float | Fraction of **all dense params** that are zero (includes biases and, for S2, the rebuilt model's smaller param total). |
| `nm_pattern` | str/null | S4 only, e.g. `"2:4"`. |
| `group_sparsity` | float/null | S2 only: fraction of groups removed (the frozen target's group fraction). |
| `parent_run_id` | str | The **canonical seed-0 dense training run** for this architecture (from the checkpoint metadata). |
| `checkpoint` | str/null | Path of the saved pruned post-finetune model, `checkpoints/pilot/<arm_id>.pt` (set on both rows; file exists once the run completes). |
| `per_layer` | list[dict] | One entry per eligible tensor: `name`, `shape` (dense parent shape for S1/S3/S4; rebuilt shape for S2), `numel`, `nonzero`, `sparsity`. |
| `paths` | dict | Two runtime paths (B.4), keyed `dense_zeros` and `compact`: `runtime_status` (`ok` / `unsupported:<reason>` / `dense_fallback:<reason>`), `latency` (frozen protocol), `rss_before_model_bytes`, `peak_rss_bytes`, `model_rss_delta_bytes`, and the path's size fields: `dense_zeros` → `dense_bytes` + `gzip_bytes`; `compact` → `compressed_bytes` (the compact artifact file size) and `artifact` (path). For S4 the `dense_zeros` row is the benchmarked dense fallback when the semi-structured runtime is unsupported; see `paths.compact.runtime_status`. |

`status=failed` rows carry a classified `reason`: `unsupported_backend`,
`numerical`, `bug`, `not_applicable` (plus the exception message after `:`).

## Compute (MAC estimates)

Computed from the actual model's layer shapes (works for any
Linear/Conv2d/GCNConv sizes), not hard-coded. Per single sample (per image /
per node for fmnist-MLP/CNN; full graph for GCN).

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `est_macs` | int | Total forward MACs assuming **all weights are nonzero** (dense convention). |
| `est_macs_nonzero` | int | Same count but only over weight elements that are **actually nonzero** in the loaded checkpoint. Equals `est_macs` for the dense baseline; smaller once Part B prunes weights. |
| `est_macs_sparse_input` | int/null | GCN only: `est_macs` with the layer-1 projection counted as `nnz(X) * out` instead of `N * in * out`, because Cora's node features are ~1.3% dense (sparse-input convention). Null for MLP/CNN. |
| `gcn_norm_macs` | int/null | GCN only: the degree-normalization (D^{1/2}) elementwise scaling multiplications, `2 * out * (E + N)` per GCNConv layer, reported **separately** and excluded from `est_macs`. Null for MLP/CNN. |

### MAC conventions

- **Linear(in, out):** `in * out` per token (1 per image / per node). Bias excluded.
- **Conv2d(cin, cout, k, padding):** `cin * cout * k^2 * H_out * W_out` per image
  (`H_out`/`W_out` are the actual output feature-map dims after padding). MaxPool/ReLU contribute 0.
- **GCNConv(in, out)** (torch_geometric, self-loops added): the weight is applied **once per
  node** (`X @ W`), not per edge. Per layer:
  - projection = `N * in * out` (dense-X weight product),
  - aggregation = `(E + N) * out` (weighted sum over the E directed edges plus N self-loops).
  - `est_macs` = sum over layers of (projection + aggregation); normalization scales go in `gcn_norm_macs`.
  - `est_macs_sparse_input` = `est_macs` but with the layer-1 projection replaced by `nnz(X) * out`.
  - For Cora: N = 2,708, E = 10,556, in1 = 1,433, out1 = 16, in2 = 16, out2 = 7 →
    `est_macs` ≈ 6.27e7, `est_macs_nonzero` = `est_macs` (dense),
    `est_macs_sparse_input` ≈ 1.0e6.

### Dense seed-0 reference values

- MLP: `est_macs` = 234,752 per image.
- CNN: `est_macs` = 1,697,280 per image (conv2 output is 10×10: 28 → conv1 pad2 → 28 →
  pool → 14 → conv2 5×5 no pad → 10 → pool → 5).

## Memory

Measured in a fresh subprocess that (1) imports torch + loads the **small fixed
benchmark input** (never the 55k training tensor), records `rss_before_model_bytes`,
(2) loads the checkpoint and runs a few forwards, recording the peak.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rss_before_model_bytes` | int | RSS after imports + benchmark-input load, **before** loading the model. |
| `peak_rss_bytes` | int | Peak RSS observed while loading the model and running forwards. |
| `model_rss_delta_bytes` | int | `peak_rss_bytes - rss_before_model_bytes` — the memory attributable to the model + activations. |

## Latency

Frozen protocol: `torch.inference_mode()`, `model.eval()`, 20 warm-up + 200 timed
iterations, `time.perf_counter_ns`, median and IQR reported. Inputs are the fixed
**benchmark batch** (first 256 TEST images, inputs only) — not training images.

`latency` is a dict keyed by `batch_1` / `batch_256` (fmnist) or `full_graph` (gcn),
each with: `median_ms`, `iqr_ms`, `warmup`, `iters`, `threads`, `batch_size`.

## Provenance

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `wall_time_s` | float | Wall-clock seconds for the command. |
| `code_hash` | str | SHA-256 over all files under `code/` (git-free). |
| `versions` | dict | python / torch / numpy / platform versions. |
| `timestamp` | str | ISO-8601 UTC creation time. |
| `target_sparsity`, `achieved_sparsity`, `stored_precision`, `compute_precision`, `accumulator_precision` | — | 0.0 / "fp32" for the dense baseline. |

## Fixed benchmark input

`results/bench/fmnist_bench_input.pt` = first 256 TEST Fashion-MNIST images,
inputs only (no labels), saved once. `results/bench/cora_bench_input.pt` = full-graph
Cora features + edge_index. These are the latency/RSS inputs and are independent of
the 55k training tensor.

## Part C — Reduced precision (frozen 2026-11-09, before any Part C run)

### C.1 Frozen design

**Parents.** The standalone precision study starts from the canonical seed-0 dense FP32
checkpoint of each architecture. Conversion is post-training only; there is no QAT.

**Formats.** Each one is run only where the laptop backend supports it. An unsupported
format gets a classified failed/unsupported row, never a missing cell.
1. **FP16 and BF16.** Weights and inputs are cast. I will report whether each op actually
   executes in that dtype on CPU, and any upcasting, by inspecting output dtypes per layer
   and checking kernel support.
2. **Dynamic INT8.** INT8 weights with per-batch activation quantization, applied to
   Linear-type layers, on whichever quantized engine is available (`qnnpack` was the only
   engine at setup). GCN projections are included if the backend can quantize them,
   otherwise they are classified as unsupported.
3. **Static INT8 (calibrated).** INT8 weights and activations with observers calibrated on
   the subset below. It uses whichever supported flow works, and records which flow was used
   (eager, FX, or PT2E). Ops that cannot be quantized stay FP32, and are counted as such.
4. **Simulated weight-only INT4.**
   - Per-output-channel symmetric quantization to [−8, 7], with an FP32 scale per output
     channel.
   - Two values are packed per uint8 on disk.
   - At runtime the weights are dequantized to FP32 and computed in FP32. This is
     **labelled simulated/non-native**, and the dequantization cost is either inside or
     outside the timed region. That choice is recorded and applied identically everywhere.

**Required accounting per row.**
- Stored, compute, and accumulator precision.
- Actual serialized bytes on disk.
- The **fraction of MACs that truly executed in reduced precision**, computed from the
  per-layer MAC table and which layers actually ran quantized/half kernels.
- Reload equivalence: logits of the reloaded artifact vs the in-memory converted model,
  within an explicit tolerance. The tolerance is 0 for exact formats, and 1e-5 relative for
  FP32 recompute paths.

**Calibration rule (frozen).**
- Fashion-MNIST: the same 1,024-image calibration subset as S3. It comes from the
  **training** split, stratified 102–103 per class, seed 12345, saved as
  `splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy`. Only inputs are used, no labels.
- Cora: the single full-graph forward pass over all node features with the fixed graph.
  This is inputs only. No labels of any split are used, and it is the only coherent
  calibration for a transductive full-graph model.
- No validation or test labels are used anywhere in calibration.

**Best supported INT8 method per architecture (frozen rule).** Among dynamic and static
INT8 conversions of the dense parent that are supported for that architecture, choose the
one with the **higher validation accuracy**. Ties within one validation example go to the
lower batch-256 / full-graph median latency. If only one method is supported, use it.

**Sparse operating point per architecture (frozen rule, validation-based; applied after
the Part B confirmations, before any Part C run).**
- Consider the four confirmed Part B points (S1–S4) for that architecture.
- *Eligible:* mean post-fine-tune validation accuracy over confirmatory seeds 1–3 must be
  ≥ dense seed-0 validation − τ, counted in correct validation examples, with τ as in B.3.
- Among the eligible points, choose the one with the **smallest measured serialized size of
  its best compact artifact** (CSR for S1/S3, the rebuilt model for S2, the N:M pack for
  S4). This is the smallest deployable model that keeps validation accuracy. Size is a
  property of the artifact, not of test data.
- Ties within 1% of bytes go to the higher mean validation accuracy.
- If none is eligible, choose the point with the highest mean validation accuracy.
- The chosen point's **seed-0 pilot checkpoint** is the sparse FP32 parent for the
  factorial.

**Factorial (12 conditions).**
- For each architecture: dense FP32, sparse FP32, dense INT8, and sparse+INT8 (the best
  INT8 method above, applied to the sparse model).
- For mask-based sparsity I report whether zeros survive quantization (the nonzero count
  after INT8), the INT8 file size, and, where implementable, a sparse-INT8 storage size.
  The latter is labelled as runtime-unsupported if there is no sparse INT8 kernel.

### C.2 Predictions

**Format that minimizes file size: simulated INT4.** It stores about 0.5 B/weight plus one
FP32 scale per output channel, so files will be about 13–14% of FP32 for MLP/CNN. The GCN
will be slightly worse because its container overhead is proportionally larger. INT8 comes
second at about 26–28% of FP32, and FP16/BF16 at about 50%.

**Format that minimizes latency: none of the reduced formats beats FP32 at batch 1 on any
model.**
- At batch 256 I expect at most a modest INT8 gain on the MLP (dynamic) and possibly the CNN
  (static, if conv runs on qnnpack).
- FP16/BF16 will be *slower* than or equal to FP32 on this CPU, because of weak half-precision
  CPU kernels and casts.
- Simulated INT4 will be the slowest, because it pays dequantization and still computes in
  FP32.
- For the GCN, the full-graph sparse aggregation is not quantized, and the X·W projection
  stays FP32 or gets converted at a cost. I expect no reduced-precision speedup.

**Why the size winner and the latency winner need not be the same.** File size is set only
by the bits stored per weight. Latency is set by whether the backend has a **native kernel**
that computes in that dtype, plus conversion overheads: quantizing and dequantizing
activations, casts, and layout packing. For models this small, fixed dispatch overhead
dominates arithmetic. INT4 has the smallest footprint but no native compute here, so it is
the opposite of fastest.

**Accuracy.**
- FP16/BF16: < 0.1 pp change; BF16 possibly up to 0.3 pp.
- Dynamic INT8: < 0.3 pp.
- Static INT8: < 0.5 pp.
- INT4: MLP −0.5 to −1 pp, CNN −1 to −2 pp, GCN −1 to −3 pp.
- Ranking of sensitivity to precision: GCN ≥ CNN > MLP.

**Composition.**
- *Size:* sizes compose only when the sparse format carries INT8 values. With int32 indices,
  index overhead dominates, so sparse+INT8 storage beats dense INT8 only at high sparsity
  (about ≥ 80%).
- *Latency:* latency will **not** compose. There is no sparse INT8 CPU kernel, so
  sparse+INT8 runs as dense INT8 with zeros, at the same latency as dense INT8.
- *Accuracy:* the loss will be roughly additive, and small.
- *Zeros:* zeros survive symmetric INT8 weight quantization exactly, because 0 maps to 0.

### C.3 Sparse operating points (applied 2026-11-09 after the Part B confirmations, before any Part C run)

The frozen C.1 rule was applied by `scripts/select_partc.py`; the output is in
`results/partc_selection.json`. Eligibility uses mean confirmatory validation counts over
seeds 1–3. The choice among eligible points uses the measured compact bytes of the seed-0
pilot checkpoint. All 12 confirmed points were eligible.

| Arch | Selected | Compact bytes | Mean val (s1–3) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | **S1, 90%** | 193,288 | 0.8935 | S3 90% within 1% of bytes (193,416), lower val (0.8889) |
| CNN | **S1, 75%** | 239,235 | 0.9203 | S3 75% within 1% (239,363), lower val (0.9157) |
| GCN | **S3, 90%** | 21,793 | 0.7947 | S1 90% identical bytes, lower val (0.7913) |

**Consequence noted in advance.** All three operating points are *unstructured* masks.
Their measured speed advantage on this laptop is zero (CSR was 20–44× slower than dense in
Part B). So the factorial will test composition on **size** with the INT8 *dense* runtime
carrying the zeros. This follows from the frozen size-based rule; it was not chosen to
produce a particular result.

"""Frozen latency protocol (Part A.1) + analytical MAC estimates.

Latency: torch.inference_mode(), model in eval(). 20 warm-up and 200 timed
iterations, time.perf_counter_ns. Report median and IQR (q3 - q1).
The fixed benchmark input is the first 256 TEST images (inputs only, saved once
to a small file, results/bench/fmnist_bench_input.pt) — NOT training images.
Batch sizes 1 and 256 for Fashion-MNIST; one full-graph forward for Cora.

Memory: the RSS subprocess does not load the 55k training tensor. It loads the
small fixed bench input and the checkpoint, and reports
rss_before_model_bytes (after imports + input load), peak_rss_bytes and
model_rss_delta_bytes = peak - before.

MAC counting (computed from the ACTUAL model's layer shapes — works for any
Linear / Conv2d / GCNConv sizes; nothing is hard-coded). We trace one forward
pass with hooks, and for every weight-bearing module (Linear, Conv2d, GCNConv)
count the MACs its weight performs per single sample:

- Linear(in, out):   each weight element multiplies one input per token;
  MACs = numel(W) * tokens (tokens = 1 here, i.e. per image / per node).
- Conv2d(cin, cout, k): each weight element is applied at every output-pixel
  position; MACs = numel(W) * H_out * W_out per image.
- GCNConv(in, out):   GCNConv computes X @ W ONCE per node (not per edge) and
  then aggregates over the augmented adjacency A' = A + I (self-loops). Per
  layer:
      projection   = N * in * out       (the dense-X weight product)
      aggregation  = (E + N) * out      (weighted sum over the E+N A' entries)
  where N = node count, E = directed edges (A' adds N self-loops).
  The degree-normalization factors D^{1/2} are elementwise scales and add
  ~2 * out * (E+N) multiplications; these are reported separately under
  `gcn_norm_macs` and are NOT part of est_macs.

Two MAC fields are emitted for every model:
- est_macs          : MACs assuming ALL weights are nonzero (dense convention).
                      For GCN this is the dense-X total above.
- est_macs_nonzero  : the same count but only for weight elements that are
                      actually nonzero in the loaded checkpoint (this is what
                      matters once Part B makes the model physically sparse).
GCN additionally reports:
- est_macs_sparse_input : est_macs with the layer-1 projection counted as
                      nnz(X)*out instead of N*in*out, because Cora's features
                      are ~1.3% dense (sparse-input convention).

For the dense seed-0 baselines every weight is nonzero, so
est_macs == est_macs_nonzero.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .evaln import load_checkpoint
from .models import count_params, dense_bytes, gzip_bytes, raw_tensor_bytes
from .util import (
    BENCH_DIR,
    ROOT,
    base_record,
    prior_bench_run_ids,
    run_wall_timer,
    set_threads,
    write_run_record,
)

WARMUP = 20
TIMED = 200
BATCH_SIZES = [1, 256]
FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT = BENCH_DIR / "fmnist_bench_input.pt"
CORAL_BENCH_INPUT = BENCH_DIR / "cora_bench_input.pt"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fixed benchmark inputs (inputs only). Saved once, reused by the main process
# and the RSS subprocess so neither ever loads the 55k training tensor.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _ensure_fmnist_bench_input() -> torch.Tensor:
    """First 256 TEST images, inputs only (no labels). Saved once."""
    if FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT.exists():
        return torch.load(FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    _, _, _, _, te_x, _, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
    BENCH_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    torch.save(te_x[:256].contiguous(), FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT)
    return torch.load(FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)


def _ensure_cora_bench_input() -> dict:
    """Full-graph Cora features + edge_index (inputs only). Saved once."""
    if CORAL_BENCH_INPUT.exists():
        return torch.load(CORAL_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    data = load_cora()
    BENCH_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    payload = {"x": data.x.contiguous(), "edge_index": data.edge_index.contiguous()}
    torch.save(payload, CORAL_BENCH_INPUT)
    return torch.load(CORAL_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)


def load_bench_input(architecture: str):
    """Return the fixed benchmark input: (x, edge_index). edge_index is None for
    fmnist; x is the (256,1,28,28) test-image batch for fmnist and the full
    (N,in) Cora feature matrix for gcn."""
    if architecture == "gcn":
        d = _ensure_cora_bench_input()
        return d["x"], d["edge_index"]
    return _ensure_fmnist_bench_input(), None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MAC estimation from actual layer shapes (no hard-coded numbers).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _weight_of(mod):
    """The parameter a module multiplies the input by (GCNConv holds it in a
    nested Linear as `lin.weight`; Linear/Conv2d hold it as `.weight`)."""
    w = getattr(mod, "weight", None)
    if w is None and hasattr(mod, "lin"):
        w = mod.lin.weight
    return w


def _mac_entries(model, x, edge_index=None):
    """Run one forward pass, recording (weight numel, weight nnz, out_ch,
    tokens) for each Linear / Conv2d / GCNConv in forward order.

    B1b: `tokens` is always the SINGLE-SAMPLE convention (1 image / 1 node
    spatial position), independent of the batch size of `x` — callers pass
    the actual forward input for shape discovery, but per-image MACs are what
    `est_macs`/`est_macs_nonzero` report (full graph for GCN, N = node count)."""
    from torch_geometric.nn import GCNConv

    model.eval()
    entries = []
    hooks = []
    for name, mod in model.named_modules():
        if isinstance(mod, (nn.Linear, nn.Conv2d)) or type(mod).__name__ == "GCNConv":
            def _hook(m, inp, out, _mod=mod, _name=name):
                w = _weight_of(_mod)
                if w.dim() == 4:  # Conv2d: per image = 1 per output pixel
                    tokens = int(out.shape[-2] * out.shape[-1])
                elif type(_mod).__name__ == "GCNConv":
                    # GCN: per full graph = N nodes (forward is one graph)
                    tokens = int(out.shape[0])
                else:            # Linear: per image = 1 token
                    tokens = 1
                entries.append({
                    "name": _name,
                    "type": type(_mod).__name__,
                    "numel": int(w.numel()),
                    "nnz": int(w.count_nonzero()),
                    "out_ch": int(out.shape[-1]),
                    "tokens": tokens,
                })
            hooks.append(mod.register_forward_hook(_hook))
    try:
        with torch.inference_mode():
            if edge_index is not None:
                model(x, edge_index)
            else:
                model(x[:1])
    finally:
        for h in hooks:
            h.remove()
    return entries


def estimate_macs(model, x, edge_index=None, x_nnz: int | None = None) -> dict:
    """Analytical MAC estimate computed from the model's actual layer shapes.

    Returns dict with est_macs, est_macs_nonzero, gcn_norm_macs and
    est_macs_sparse_input (GCN only, else None).
    """
    entries = _mac_entries(model, x, edge_index)

    is_gcn = edge_index is not None
    if is_gcn:
        N = int(x.shape[0])
        E = int(edge_index.shape[1])          # directed edges (no self-loops yet)
        E_plus_N = E + N                      # A' = A + I
        norm_macs = 0
    else:
        N = E_plus_N = None
        norm_macs = 0

    est = 0
    est_nz = 0
    est_sparse = None  # computed on first GCNConv layer, else None (non-GCN)
    for e in entries:
        if e["type"] == "GCNConv":
            proj = e["numel"] * e["tokens"]              # N*in*out (dense-X)
            proj_nz = e["nnz"] * e["tokens"]             # nonzero weights only
            agg = E_plus_N * e["out_ch"]
            if est_sparse is None and x_nnz is not None:
                est_sparse = (x_nnz * e["out_ch"]) + agg
            else:
                est_sparse += proj + agg
            est += proj + agg
            est_nz += proj_nz + agg
            norm_macs += 2 * e["out_ch"] * E_plus_N
        else:  # Linear / Conv2d
            est += e["numel"] * e["tokens"]
            est_nz += e["nnz"] * e["tokens"]
            if est_sparse is not None:
                est_sparse += e["numel"] * e["tokens"]

    return {
        "est_macs": est,
        "est_macs_nonzero": est_nz,
        "est_macs_sparse_input": (est_sparse if is_gcn and est_sparse is not None else None),
        "gcn_norm_macs": norm_macs,
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Timing (frozen protocol) and peak-RSS subprocess.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _time_batch(model, x, batch_size: int) -> dict:
    """Frozen protocol: inference_mode, eval(), 20 warm-up / 200 timed iterations.
    A pre-allocated (batch_size, ...) view of the fixed bench input is used each
    iteration so the timed region is the model forward pass only."""
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        xb = x[:batch_size] if len(x) >= batch_size else x
        for _ in range(WARMUP):
            model(xb)
        ns = []
        for _ in range(TIMED):
            t0 = time.perf_counter_ns()
            model(xb)
            ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t0)
    ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
    q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
    return {"median_ms": float(q2), "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1)}


def _bench_peak_rss(architecture: str, seed: int) -> dict:
    """RSS measured in a fresh subprocess that (1) imports + loads the small
    fixed bench input, (2) records rss_before_model_bytes, (3) loads the
    checkpoint and runs a few forwards, recording peak_rss_bytes. Returns
    (rss_before, peak)."""
    code = f"""
import json, psutil, sys
import torch
from lab3.util import set_threads
from lab3.bench import load_bench_input
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
set_threads()
x, ei = load_bench_input("{architecture}")
proc = psutil.Process()
before = proc.memory_info().rss
m, _ = load_checkpoint("{architecture}", {seed})
m.eval()
peak = before
with torch.inference_mode():
    for _ in range(5):
        if "{architecture}" == "gcn":
            m(x, ei)
        else:
            m(x[:256])
        peak = max(peak, proc.memory_info().rss)
print(json.dumps({{"before": int(before), "peak": int(peak)}}))
"""
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, cwd=str(ROOT),
        env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(ROOT / "code")},
    )
    out = json.loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    return out


def bench(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    set_threads()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="bench")
    rec["seed"] = seed
    try:
        model, meta = load_checkpoint(architecture, seed)
        # Linkage: parent run is the training run that produced this checkpoint.
        rec["parent_run_id"] = meta.get("run_id")
        rec["supersedes"] = prior_bench_run_ids(architecture, seed)

        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)
        rec["raw_tensor_bytes"] = raw_tensor_bytes(model)
        # P1: gzip_bytes = gzip-9 size of the dense state_dict file, reported for
        # EVERY run (dense included). compressed_bytes is reserved for the
        # compact-export artifact (Part B path 2); null for dense.
        rec["gzip_bytes"] = gzip_bytes(model)
        rec["compressed_bytes"] = None
        rec["best_epoch"] = meta.get("best_epoch")
        rec["val_acc"] = meta.get("val_acc")

        x, ei = load_bench_input(architecture)
        model.eval()

        if architecture == "gcn":
            with torch.inference_mode():
                for _ in range(WARMUP):
                    model(x, ei)
                ns = []
                for _ in range(TIMED):
                    t_start = time.perf_counter_ns()
                    model(x, ei)
                    ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t_start)
            ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
            q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
            rec["latency"] = {
                "full_graph": {
                    "median_ms": float(q2),
                    "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1),
                    "warmup": WARMUP,
                    "iters": TIMED,
                    "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
                    "batch_size": "full_graph",
                }
            }
            macs = estimate_macs(model, x, ei, x_nnz=int(x.count_nonzero()))
        else:
            lat = {}
            for bs in BATCH_SIZES:
                lat[f"batch_{bs}"] = _time_batch(model, x, bs)
                lat[f"batch_{bs}"].update({"warmup": WARMUP, "iters": TIMED,
                                           "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
                                           "batch_size": bs})
            rec["latency"] = lat
            macs = estimate_macs(model, x[:1], None)

        rec["est_macs"] = macs["est_macs"]
        rec["est_macs_nonzero"] = macs["est_macs_nonzero"]
        rec["est_macs_sparse_input"] = macs["est_macs_sparse_input"]
        rec["gcn_norm_macs"] = macs["gcn_norm_macs"]

        rss = _bench_peak_rss(architecture, seed)
        rec["rss_before_model_bytes"] = rss["before"]
        rec["peak_rss_bytes"] = rss["peak"]
        rec["model_rss_delta_bytes"] = rss["peak"] - rss["before"]

        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec
    except Exception as e:
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        write_run_record(rec)
        raise

"""Evaluation of a saved dense checkpoint (test set only, no weight updates)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import time

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .models import build_model, count_params, dense_bytes
from .util import (
    CHECKPOINTS_DIR,
    base_record,
    run_wall_timer,
    set_seed,
    set_threads,
    write_run_record,
)


def load_checkpoint(architecture: str, seed: int):
    path = CHECKPOINTS_DIR / f"{architecture}_seed{seed}.pt"
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no checkpoint at {path}; run train first")
    payload = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    model = build_model(architecture)
    model.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
    return model, payload["metadata"]


def eval(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Evaluate the saved seed checkpoint on val+test. Never updates weights:
    inference_mode + eval() only. Appends a run record."""
    set_threads()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="eval")
    rec["seed"] = seed
    try:
        model, meta = load_checkpoint(architecture, seed)
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)
        rec["best_epoch"] = meta.get("best_epoch")
        rec["val_acc"] = meta.get("val_acc")
        rec["val_loss"] = meta.get("val_loss")

        if architecture == "gcn":
            data = load_cora()
            model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
                va = out[data.lm_val]
                te = out[data.lm_test]
                rec["val_loss"] = float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(va, data.y[data.lm_val]).item())
                rec["val_acc"] = float((va.argmax(dim=1) == data.y[data.lm_val]).float().mean().item())
                rec["test_acc"] = float((te.argmax(dim=1) == data.y[data.lm_test]).float().mean().item())
        else:
            tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
            model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                for x, y, kind in ((va_x, va_y, "val"), (te_x, te_y, "test")):
                    n = len(y)
                    correct = 0
                    loss_sum = 0.0
                    bs = 1024
                    for i in range(0, n, bs):
                        xb, yb = x[i:i + bs], y[i:i + bs]
                        out = model(xb)
                        loss_sum += float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, yb, reduction="sum").item())
                        correct += int((out.argmax(dim=1) == yb).sum().item())
                    if kind == "val":
                        rec["val_acc"] = correct / n
                        rec["val_loss"] = loss_sum / n
                    else:
                        rec["test_acc"] = correct / n

        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec
    except Exception as e:
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        write_run_record(rec)
        raise

"""Part B path 2 — genuinely compact runtime modules (predictions.md B.4).

S1/S3: dense-shaped math executed as CSR sparse x dense matmul.

B1b review (frozen design, corrected implementation):

* CSR orientation: every weight W [out, in] is stored as a CSR matrix with
  shape (out, in). The optimized CPU path is ``torch.sparse.mm`` in the
  **sparse x dense** orientation, so each layer computes
  ``y = (W_csr @ x^T)^T`` (never ``x @ W_csr^T``, which dispatches dense x
  sparse and is not the optimized path).
* Index dtype: CSR indices use int32 when ``torch.sparse.mm`` supports it on
  CPU (probed once at import; ``csr_index_dtype`` is recorded per artifact).
  The equivalent default int64 layout size is recorded as
  ``csr_int64_bytes``.
* CSRConv2d: no Python loop over the batch. ``F.unfold`` produces columns
  (B, in*k*k, L); reshaping to (in*k*k, B*L) and one sparse mm computes the
  whole batch (pixel order of F.unfold is (y, x) inside each image, which is
  exactly Conv2d's output order).
* CSRGCNConv: a GCNConv subclass in which ONLY the per-edge projection
  differs (``message`` does the sparse x dense projection); the
  gcn_norm edge-weight computation, propagation and aggregation are exactly
  the PyG GCNConv code (same ``propagate``/``gcn_norm``/aggr_module).
* S4: the packed file stores only the kept values (row-major) plus ONE uint8
  in-block position per kept value; row and block are implied by the fixed
  N:M pattern and the frozen partial-block ceil rule.
  ``nm_bitpacked_bytes_theoretical`` = values*4 + ceil(nnz*ceil(log2 M)/8)
  + biases is recorded and labelled theoretical.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import os
import warnings

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=".*Sparse CSR.*")
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=".*Sparse invariant.*")

from torch_geometric.nn import GCNConv


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CSR construction (orientation (out, in); sparse x dense via torch.sparse.mm)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _csr_components(w: torch.Tensor, index_dtype: torch.dtype):
    """Dense [out, in] -> (crow, col, values) row-major CSR components."""
    rows, cols = w.nonzero().t()
    crow = torch.zeros(w.shape[0] + 1, dtype=index_dtype)
    if rows.numel():
        cnt = torch.bincount(rows, minlength=w.shape[0]).to(index_dtype)
        crow[1:] = cnt.cumsum(0)
    values = w[rows, cols].contiguous()
    return crow, cols.to(index_dtype).contiguous(), values


def dense_to_csr(w: torch.Tensor, index_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None):
    """Dense [out, in] -> CSR (out, in) components (indptr, indices, values, size)."""
    if index_dtype is None:
        index_dtype = CSR_INDEX_DTYPE
    indptr, indices, values = _csr_components(w, index_dtype)
    return indptr, indices, values, list(w.shape)


def _probe_csr_index_dtype() -> torch.dtype:
    """Probe whether torch supports int32 CSR indices for sparse.mm on CPU.

    B1b: on this torch build the CSR tensor object itself is NOT deepcopy
    -able (the CSR impl forbids storage access; ``copy.deepcopy`` on a CSR
    tensor raises). Since the eval protocol (tests + GCN cache clearing)
    deepcopies the compact model, we additionally require int32 support to
    fall back cleanly: prefer int32 (smaller artifact, supported); the
    default int64 layout size is recorded separately as csr_int64_bytes."""
    try:
        w = torch.arange(12, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(3, 4)
        w[0, 3] = 0.0
        crow, col, vals = _csr_components(w, torch.int32)
        csr = torch.sparse_csr_tensor(crow, col, vals, size=list(w.shape), dtype=w.dtype)
        x = torch.randn(4, 2)
        y = torch.sparse.mm(csr, x)
        assert torch.allclose(y, w @ x, atol=1e-5)
        return torch.int32
    except Exception:
        return torch.int64


# CSR_INDEX_DTYPE is the index dtype used for the compact runtime modules and
# recorded as `csr_index_dtype` on the artifact.
CSR_INDEX_DTYPE = _probe_csr_index_dtype()


def csr_tensor(crow, col, values, size) -> torch.Tensor:
    return torch.sparse_csr_tensor(crow, col, values, size=size, dtype=values.dtype)


def csr_from_components(d: dict) -> torch.Tensor:
    return csr_tensor(d["indptr"], d["indices"], d["values"], size=d["size"])


def csr_int64_bytes(crow, col, values, size) -> int:
    """Size of the equivalent DEFAULT int64 CSR layout (values + int64
    indptr/indices), payload only."""
    return (values.numel() * values.element_size()
            + crow.numel() * 8 + col.numel() * 8)


def s4_bitpacked_bytes_theoretical(pack: dict) -> int:
    """THEORETICAL (labelled) bit-packed size of one S4 weight tensor: kept
    values as FP32 (4 B) + ONE bit-packed in-block position per kept value
    (ceil(log2 M) bits, packed, ceiling to whole bytes) — row/block implied
    by the fixed pattern + partial-block ceil rule. Biases are accounted for
    separately by the caller via pack['bias_bytes'] (sum over the model)."""
    m = pack["m"]
    nnz = pack["values"].numel()
    value_bytes = nnz * 4
    if nnz == 0:
        pos_bytes = 0
    else:
        bits = int(math.ceil(math.log2(m))) if m > 1 else 1
        pos_bytes = int(math.ceil(nnz * bits / 8))
    return value_bytes + pos_bytes


def save_csr(w: torch.Tensor, path: str) -> int:
    """Save the CSR of dense [out, in] weight `w` to disk; returns file size."""
    indptr, indices, values, size = dense_to_csr(w)
    torch.save({"values": values, "indptr": indptr, "indices": indices,
                "size": size, "csr_index_dtype": str(CSR_INDEX_DTYPE),
                "csr_int64_bytes": csr_int64_bytes(indptr, indices, values, size)},
               path)
    return os.path.getsize(path)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compact runtime modules
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class CSRLinear(nn.Module):
    """y = (W_csr @ x^T)^T + b, W_csr shape (out, in); sparse x dense.

    B1b: the CSR tensor is rebuilt from its dense weight on the first forward
    (and after a train-mode forward) rather than kept as a buffer: the CSR
    tensor object is not deepcopy-able in this torch build (the CSR impl
    forbids storage access), and the eval protocol deepcopies the model.
    The weight is therefore held as a dense buffer (the same zeros as the
    dense_zeros path) and converted on demand; the conversion is cached per
    (data_ptr, nnz) so repeated forwards are cheap."""

    def __init__(self, w_dense: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor | None):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("w_dense", w_dense.detach().clone())
        self.register_buffer("bias", bias)
        self.out_features = w_dense.size(0)
        self.in_features = w_dense.size(1)
        self._w_csr: torch.Tensor | None = None
        self._w_key: tuple | None = None

    def _csr(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        key = (self.w_dense.data_ptr(), int(self.w_dense.count_nonzero()))
        if self._w_csr is None or self._w_key != key:
            crow, col, vals = _csr_components(self.w_dense, CSR_INDEX_DTYPE)
            self._w_csr = torch.sparse_csr_tensor(
                crow, col, vals, size=list(self.w_dense.shape),
                dtype=self.w_dense.dtype)
            self._w_key = key
        return self._w_csr

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        y = torch.sparse.mm(self._csr(), x.t()).t()
        if self.bias is not None:
            y = y + self.bias
        return y


class CSRConv2d(nn.Module):
    """CSR matmul conv, no Python loop over the batch: unfold once, reshape
    the columns to (in*k*k, B*L) and run ONE sparse mm (sparse x dense).
    B1b: holds the dense (zeroed) weight and rebuilds the CSR on demand (the
    CSR tensor object is not deepcopy-able in this torch build)."""

    def __init__(self, w_dense_flat: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor,
                 kernel_size: int, padding: int, out_spatial: tuple[int, int] | None = None):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("w_dense", w_dense_flat.detach().clone())
        self.register_buffer("bias", bias)
        self.k = kernel_size
        self.pad = padding
        self.out_spatial = out_spatial
        self._w_csr: torch.Tensor | None = None
        self._w_key: tuple | None = None

    def _csr(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        key = (self.w_dense.data_ptr(), int(self.w_dense.count_nonzero()))
        if self._w_csr is None or self._w_key != key:
            crow, col, vals = _csr_components(self.w_dense, CSR_INDEX_DTYPE)
            self._w_csr = torch.sparse_csr_tensor(
                crow, col, vals, size=list(self.w_dense.shape),
                dtype=self.w_dense.dtype)
            self._w_key = key
        return self._w_csr

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        b, cin, h, wd = x.shape
        kk = self.k
        cols = F.unfold(x, (kk, kk), padding=self.pad)      # (B, in*k*k, L)
        cols = cols.permute(1, 0, 2).reshape(self.w_dense.size(1), -1)
        y = torch.sparse.mm(self._csr(), cols)              # (out, B*L)
        if self.out_spatial is not None:
            oh, ow = self.out_spatial
        else:
            oh = ow = int(math.isqrt(y.size(1) // b))
        # F.unfold pixel order: p = (y * ow + x) inside each image
        y = y.reshape(self.w_dense.size(0), b, oh, ow).permute(1, 0, 2, 3)
        return y + self.bias.view(1, -1, 1, 1)


class CSRGCNConv(GCNConv):
    """GCNConv in which ONLY the projection differs from the dense path.

    The dense GCNConv computes ``x = self.lin(x)`` (x @ W^T + lin bias-free)
    and then runs ``propagate`` (gcn_norm normalization + message +
    aggregation). Here ``self.lin`` is replaced by a CSR projection that
    computes ``x @ W^T = (W_csr @ x^T)^T`` via the optimized sparse x dense
    ``torch.sparse.mm`` path. ``propagate`` (normalization, message and
    aggregation) is the untouched PyG GCNConv code, so the latency contrast
    isolates the sparse projection."""

    def __init__(self, w_dense: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor,
                 in_channels: int, out_channels: int):
        super().__init__(in_channels, out_channels, add_self_loops=True,
                         normalize=True)
        with torch.no_grad():
            self.bias.data = bias.detach().clone()
        # Replace the dense projection ``lin`` (bias=False in GCNConv) with the
        # CSR projection. Only the projection differs; message/aggregation are
        # the PyG identity/scatter code.
        self.lin = CSRLinear(w_dense, self.lin.bias)
        # B1b: GCNConv.__init__ registers a `cached` flag; PyG's message
        # passing reads it via attribute access (not in __dict__), so it is
        # harmless; nothing to drop.
        self.w_dense_ref = None  # not used; kept for clarity

    def forward(self, x, edge_index, edge_weight=None):
        # Inherited PyG GCNConv.forward: x = self.lin(x) [CSR projection],
        # gcn_norm normalization + propagate + bias. No override needed.
        return GCNConv.forward(self, x, edge_index, edge_weight)

    def forward(self, x, edge_index, edge_weight=None):
        # Inherited PyG GCNConv.forward: x = self.lin(x) [CSR projection],
        # gcn_norm normalization + propagate + bias. No override needed.
        return GCNConv.forward(self, x, edge_index, edge_weight)


def clear_gcn_caches(model: nn.Module) -> None:
    """Clear PyG message-passing ``_cached*`` attributes (GCN caches the
    normalized edge index on the module during train-mode forwards)."""
    for mod in model.modules():
        for attr in list(vars(mod)):
            if attr.startswith("_cached"):
                setattr(mod, attr, None)


def reassemble_packed(pack: dict) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Invert s4_packed (bit-exact). The packed file stores the kept values
    in row-major order plus ONE uint8 in-block position per kept value; the
    row and block of each value are implied by the fixed N:M pattern and the
    frozen partial-block ceil rule (per-row keep counts)."""
    n, m, L, shape = pack["n"], pack["m"], pack["row_len"], tuple(pack["shape"])
    R = shape[0]
    r = L % m
    n_full = L // m
    n_blocks = n_full + (1 if r else 0)
    keep_per_block = [n] * n_full
    if r:
        keep_per_block.append(math.ceil(n * r / m))
    per_row = sum(keep_per_block)

    # per-block start offsets, in row-major block order
    starts = []
    pos = 0
    for kb in keep_per_block:
        starts.append(pos)
        pos += kb
    block_starts = torch.tensor(starts, dtype=torch.long)

    k = torch.arange(pack["n_kept"]) if "n_kept" in pack else torch.arange(pack["values"].numel())
    row = k // per_row
    block_in_row = k % per_row
    # B1b: kept values are emitted in BLOCK-MAJOR order (per row: block 0's
    # kept values in increasing in-block column, then block 1's, ...). The
    # in-block column is the ACTUAL column within the block (stored as one
    # uint8 per kept value), so column = block_flat_start + in_block_column.
    # (Using the rank within the block would be wrong because the kept set is
    # the N largest-magnitude positions, which are NOT the first N columns.)
    # B1b fix: use side="right" so that bir == block_starts[b] maps to block b
    # (not b+1). The default side="left" gives the first index where
    # block_starts[i] >= bir, which for bir == block_starts[b] returns b,
    # but for bir == block_starts[b] + 1 (the second value of block b) it
    # returns b+1, which is wrong. side="right" gives the first index where
    # block_starts[i] > bir, which for bir in [block_starts[b], block_starts[b+1])
    # returns b+1, so we subtract 1 to get b.
    block = torch.searchsorted(block_starts, block_in_row, side="right") - 1
    block = torch.clamp(block, max=len(keep_per_block) - 1, min=0)
    in_block = pack["in_block"].to(torch.long)
    if r:
        block_pos = torch.where(block < n_full,
                                block * m,
                                n_full * m + (block - n_full) * r)
    else:
        block_pos = block * m
    flat_idx = block_pos + in_block
    w = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=pack["values"].dtype)
    flat = w.view(w.shape[0], -1)
    flat[row, flat_idx] = pack["values"]
    return w


class DenseS4Module(nn.Module):
    """S4 dense fallback: weight reassembled from the packed N:M file
    (kept values + per-value in-block position) into zeros."""

    def __init__(self, dense_w: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor | None, kind: str):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("w", dense_w.detach().clone())
        self.register_buffer("bias", bias)
        self.kind = kind

    def forward(self, x, edge_index=None):
        raise NotImplementedError


class CompactModel(nn.Module):
    """Wraps a dense parent's state into the compact runtime form.

    `kind`: 'csr' (S1/S3) or 's4' (S4 dense fallback)."""

    def __init__(self, architecture: str, state: dict, kind: str):
        super().__init__()
        from .models import build_model
        self.arch = architecture
        self.kind = kind
        parent = build_model(architecture)
        parent.load_state_dict(state)
        self._build(parent)

    def _build(self, parent: nn.Module) -> None:
        from torch_geometric.nn import GCNConv

        cls = parent.__class__.__name__

        def lin(w_dense, bias):
            # stored [out, in]; the CSR projection computes (W_csr @ x^T)^T.
            # B1b: pass the dense (zeroed) weight; the CSR tensor is built on
            # demand (CSR tensors are not deepcopy-able in this torch build).
            return CSRLinear(w_dense.detach().clone(), bias)

        if cls == "MLP":
            self.m = nn.Sequential(
                lin(parent.net[0].weight, parent.net[0].bias),
                nn.ReLU(),
                lin(parent.net[2].weight, parent.net[2].bias),
                nn.ReLU(),
                lin(parent.net[4].weight, parent.net[4].bias),
            )
        elif cls == "CNN":
            # conv weight (out, in, k, k) -> CSR (out, in*k*k)
            c1, c2 = parent.conv1, parent.conv2
            self.m = nn.Sequential(
                CSRConv2d(c1.weight.detach().clone().flatten(1),
                          c1.bias, 5, 2, out_spatial=(28, 28)),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.MaxPool2d(2),
                CSRConv2d(c2.weight.detach().clone().flatten(1),
                          c2.bias, 5, 0, out_spatial=(10, 10)),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            )
            self.flatten = nn.Flatten(1)
            self.m2 = nn.Sequential(
                lin(parent.fc1.weight, parent.fc1.bias),
                nn.ReLU(),
                lin(parent.fc2.weight, parent.fc2.bias),
            )
        elif cls == "GCN":
            # GCNConv.lin.weight is stored [out, in]; the CSR projection uses
            # (W_csr @ x^T)^T so pass the stored [out, in] matrix directly.
            c1, c2 = parent.conv1, parent.conv2
            self.m = nn.Sequential(
                CSRGCNConv(c1.lin.weight.detach().clone(),
                           c1.bias, c1.in_channels, c1.out_channels),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.5),
                CSRGCNConv(c2.lin.weight.detach().clone(),
                           c2.bias, c2.in_channels, c2.out_channels),
            )
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"CompactModel: unsupported {cls}")

    def forward(self, x, edge_index=None):
        if self.arch == "gcn":
            return self._gcn(x, edge_index)
        if self.arch == "mlp":
            return self.m(x.flatten(1))
        x = self.m(x)
        return self.m2(self.flatten(x))

    def _gcn(self, x: torch.Tensor, edge_index: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # PyG message passing caches the normalized edge index on the module
        # (base GCNConv) during train-mode forwards; evaluation must use a
        # clean cache, exactly as the dense path's _fresh/clear protocol does.
        clear_gcn_caches(self)
        x = self.m[0](x, edge_index)
        x = self.m[1](x)
        x = self.m[2](x)
        x = self.m[3](x, edge_index)
        return x
